_comment: Task 6's canned tool-signals.json (spec 4.7): driven through the real merge,
verify_prompts and apply chain over the service-py corpus fixture, rather than
dispatched directly against tool_candidates/corroborate_with_tools as
TestTierProducerInvariant does -- so this file proves the fact-class producer
route reaches a tier through the disk-read path merge() actually uses in
production, and that every other candidate the same run raises (28 scout
candidates, 9 rule findings) still does not.
Every file named below is real in the service-py fixture tree. osv-scanner
targets requirements.txt, the fixture's one lockfile. gitleaks targets
src/pay/ledger.py, a file with no existing security finding of its own, so its
untiered candidate is easy to isolate. hadolint targets README.md: the
fixture's one real Dockerfile already carries a pipeline-infra rule finding
(container.unversioned-install), which would absorb a hadolint fact into that
finding's confirmed_by instead of raising a new one -- README.md has no
pipeline-infra rule finding, so the fact raises its own untiered candidate and
exercises the branch the corpus goldens never reach. jscpd targets
src/pay/ledger.py too, but as an inference signal (fact: false) on the
*second* evidence item of the fixture's one duplication candidate (whose
primary evidence is src/pay/refund.py): a corroboration match that only
checked a candidate's primary evidence file would silently miss it. lizard
names complex-units, a family with zero candidates anywhere in this fixture
(both complex-units.json and god-classes.json scouts are empty), so its
signal is guaranteed to corroborate nothing -- the no-match path.
